issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) and the classes (e.g., Seal, Goat) implement 'Dairy' rather than 'Milkable'. Additionally, solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java exists but is empty. This type/name mismatch between the expected interface name and the solution implementation will confuse students and prevent straightforward implementation or testing that expects a 'Milkable' interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across artifacts. Either (A) rename Dairy.java to Milkable.java and have all animal classes implement Milkable, and remove or populate any Milkable.java placeholder; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to use the name 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Ensure the interface file contains the method signature String messageOnMilk() and that all classes implement the same interface name as specified in the problem.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (which defines messageOnMilk()) and the animal classes implement 'Dairy'. Additionally, the solution repository contains an empty Milkable.java file. This name mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) breaks the one-to-one mapping of the conceptual 'milkable' interface across artifacts and will confuse students and cause integration/compilation issues when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update the file name to Milkable.java) so it matches the problem statement and template. Ensure the interface declares messageOnMilk(), remove the empty Milkable.java placeholder, and update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable. Alternatively, if 'Dairy' is preferred, update the problem statement and template to reference 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'.
